~1T total / ~52B active parameters : granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.

items.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
items.summary:
The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group.

We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series.

We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

items.title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
items.summary:
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $χ$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$.

To the character $χ$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_χ=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $χ$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_χ$.

We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition.

As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}χ$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

items.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on Kähler manifolds
items.summary: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected Kähler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

items.title: Alice & Bob Estimates 22,593 Qubits to Break RSA-2048
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Alice & Bob researchers estimate that running Shor’s algorithm against RSA-2048 would require 22,593 physical cat qubits and 3.14 days on fault-tolerant superconducting quantum hardware.

The study estimates that attacking the 256-bit elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem would require 29,588 physical qubits and 61.8 minutes, with the results based on cat-qubit hardware, LDPC-cat codes and a redesigned adder.

The estimates are theoretical resource projections rather than demonstrations of cryptographic attacks, and Alice & Bob recommends that organizations begin migrating to post-quantum cryptography as research continues to reduce projected hardware requirements.

PRESS RELEASE — Alice & Bob, a leader in fault-tolerant quantum computing, sets a record low for the total quantum resources (qubits multiplied by runtime) required to run Shor’s algorithm on today’s encryption. Its cat-qubit architecture needs 40 times fewer physical qubits than Google Quantum AI’s Craig Gidney 2025 estimate to break RSA-2048 ( arxiv).

In the paper “Shor’s algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days” (IACR ePrint) researchers estimate the resources to break the following systems on fault-tolerant superconducting cat-qubit hardware:

RSA-2048: 22,593 physical qubits, 3.14 days. RSA relies on the difficulty of factoring large integers. It is one of the world’s most widely used public-key systems, securing much of the internet, from online banking to email and digital signatures.

items.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
items.summary:
Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds.

Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts.

In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension.

For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag.

We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

items.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
items.summary:
We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface.

Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve.

Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

items.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
items.summary:
We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix.

The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$.

For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

items.title: One Vector or Many? Clustered Optimal-Transport Steering under Quantization
items.summary:
Activation steering changes what a language model generates by editing its hidden states at inference time. Its most common form adds one vector, the difference of class means (DiM), to every hidden state. CHaRS (concept heterogeneity-aware representation steering) uses optimal transport instead: an entropic plan pairs the clusters of the two classes, and each hidden state moves along a mixture of the cluster displacements, weighted toward its nearest clusters.

We study this family of clustered optimal-transport maps for toxicity mitigation in Gemma-2-2B and Granite-3.1-2B, and ask what the plan adds to DiM and whether that survives INT8 and NF4 quantization. We prove an identity: whatever the plan, the displacements averaged with the cluster sizes as weights equal DiM, so a clustered map can differ from DiM only for tokens whose routing weights depart from the cluster sizes. In the CHaRS protocol they stay close, and CHaRS is statistically equivalent to Mean-AcT, which adds DiM at every layer, in all eight pre-specified equivalence tests.

A variant fitted on individual tokens, which routes each token mainly to its nearest clusters, leaves 37-39% less toxicity than DiM on Gemma and 51-61% less on Granite at steering strength 3 (toxic-bert), where DiM already removes 76-85% of it. Two other toxicity classifiers confirm the gain on Granite, but on Gemma only one does. At equal strength the variant has somewhat higher perplexity, but at matched toxicity it is slightly more fluent than DiM.

Yet a nearly constant map from the same clusters also leaves about 30% less toxicity, so the role of treating tokens differently remains open. Under INT8 and NF4 the variant still leaves less toxicity than DiM, and transferring it from full precision to the NF4 model instead of refitting it adds no significant toxicity after correction for multiple tests.

items.title: Identifying Logical Operations from Syndrome Histories for qLDPC Codes
items.summary:
Syndrome histories are normally used to detect and correct errors in fault-tolerant quantum computation, but they can also reveal information about the logical operations executed during computation. We study logical-operation identification using syndrome histories alone or together with other classical measurement outcomes.

We develop an exact inference method and a scalable approximation that account for unknown circuit faults and ideal measurement randomness. We evaluate automorphisms, logical Pauli measurements, T injections, and logical circuits combining these instructions on \([[18,4,2]]\) and \([[72,12,6]]\) bivariate bicycle (BB) codes under multiple noise models and error rates.

A single logical instruction can be identified with over 94\% accuracy under circuit-level noise with error rates between \(10^ {-5} \) and \(10^{-3}\). We also achieve over 99\% accuracy for automorphism-based logical circuits and 78.32\% for logical circuits combining all three instructions.

We further analyze identification ambiguities arising from insufficient or indistinguishable measurement information, fault timing, and approximation inference. Together, these results extend the role of syndromes beyond error decoding to identifying executed logical operations and circuits during fault-tolerant quantum computation.

They also suggest that access to syndrome histories and related classical measurement outcomes may unintentionally reveal information about the executed computation.

items.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
items.summary:
Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$.

On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$.

We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$.

Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category.

As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.

items.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
items.summary:
Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition.

Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems.

To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables.

The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank.

The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

items.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
items.summary:
In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space.

Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements.

Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines.

As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free.

Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.

items.title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
items.summary:
Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_μ$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor.

Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation.

We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$.

In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

items.title: A Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for degenerations
items.summary:
We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique Kähler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization.

This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry.

As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu.

We also prove an analogous result in geometric invariant theory (GIT), stating that uniform GIT height minimization of a family of points is equivalent to GIT stability, proving a converse to work of Wang, Wang-Xu and the author.

items.title: Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ngô Fibrations
items.summary:
We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ngô fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces.

We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations.

Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.

items.title: Low-Bit GDN Recurrent-State Quantization: Global Gradient-aware Allocation and Pure-Write Sliding Windows
items.summary:
Linear attention stores historical information in a recurrent state of fixed size, providing a compact memory representation for long-context inference. Reducing state precision further lowers per-request storage requirements, but quantized writeback errors enter subsequent recurrences, degrade prediction quality on long-reasoning tasks, and can be accompanied by repetitive generation and excessively long outputs.

We propose Global Gradient-aware Allocation (GGA) and the Pure-Write Sliding Window (PW) to address precision allocation and recent-information maintenance. GGA combines candidate quantization residuals with gradient sensitivity to future prediction loss to allocate head bit widths under a model-wide mixed-precision budget.

PW independently maintains recent pure writes as FP8 vector pairs, propagates them through the full GDN state transition, and merges them into the low-bit historical state only after they leave the window. Across seven evaluations on Qwen3.5-4B/9B, GGA allocation alone improves over STEPQuant@4 by 19.48/29.84 percentage points.

Adding PW-S8 yields seven-task macro-averages of 69.83%/78.63%, improving over STEPQuant@4 by 38.39/41.21 percentage points, respectively. Both precision reallocation and window maintenance improve task scores while mitigating excessively long outputs: at @6, GGA reduces mean generation length, averaged equally across tasks, by 10.45%/14.65% relative to STEPQuant; adding PW-S8 to GGA@4 further reduces mean generation length by 32.32%/36.77%.

Comparisons at similar storage budgets further show that using additional capacity to maintain recent writes yields higher task scores and shorter mean outputs than solely increasing the bit width of the accumulated state.

items.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
items.summary:
A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type.

In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space.

The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations.

The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists.

It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.

items.title: Turing LLM Post-Training: Calibrated Distillation and Efficient Dynamic-MoE Execution
items.summary:
We study post-training for dynamically routed mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, focusing on integrating independently optimized specialists while keeping consolidation efficient. Our approach combines calibrated multi-teacher on-policy distillation (C-MOPD), which matches each selected teacher on a local Top-$K$ support with teacher-wise loss normalization and clipping, with an execution path that uses post-capacity bounded-width dispatch, final-route replay, and asynchronous rollout--training overlap.

On Turing-20B-A2B, the selected model achieves a four-domain normalized integration score of 0.9988 and retains at least 90.16\% of the measured specialist gain in every domain. At matched $K=32$, the full calibration objective scores 0.9962, compared with 0.9724 without calibration and 0.9834 without clipping.

At a matched 8K response cap, the model exceeds both shared SFT and Qwen3-8B on all four reasoning-enabled mathematics and code benchmarks (unweighted mean: 85.92, versus 80.33 for Qwen3-8B and 74.21 for SFT), and improves over SFT on ten of twelve broader evaluation metrics. In a PPU-based profile, the combined execution configuration reduces consolidation step time from 398.7 to 139.3 seconds, an observed 2.86$\times$ speedup over serial execution.

These results demonstrate strong specialist integration alongside more efficient consolidation, while reflecting the complete training and execution framework rather than any single component.

items.title: Attention, Dynamic Wave and Hybrid Sequence Mixers in Language Models
items.summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on Multi-Head Attention (MHA) for sequence modeling, but scaling to long contexts is constrained by the quadratic cost of attention, motivating sub-quadratic recurrent alternatives. This paper formalizes a Dynamic Wave recurrent layer, based on input-dependent exponential damping and cosine phase modulation, and evaluates three 10.94M-parameter configurations (Pure Transformer, Pure Wave, and Hybrid Wave-Attention) on TinyStories under perplexity, latency, throughput and peak VRAM profiling up to 4096 tokens. The Hybrid configuration reaches the best perplexity, 5.95 on the full held-out split against 6.93 for the Transformer and 7.26 for Pure Wave.

The efficiency picture, however, is governed by implementation rather than by architecture. Against an unfused attention baseline, Pure Wave uses 78.7% less peak VRAM at a 4096-token context (1404.3 MB vs. 6601.6 MB); against a fused scaled-dot-product attention kernel the same comparison yields no advantage at all (1404.3 MB vs.

1403.6 MB), and in training mode Pure Wave is 8.3% more expensive than the Transformer. Likewise, hoisting elementwise terms out of the recurrence loop speeds the layer up 2.53-fold with no custom kernel, reducing its latency gap to attention from 2.48-fold to 1.12-fold. A hybrid stack is found to inherit the cost of its more expensive mixer rather than the advantage of its cheaper one, its peak VRAM matching the Pure Transformer to within 0.1%.

A closed-form memory model reproduces these measurements and predicts the context length beyond which attention overtakes the vocabulary projection. The findings indicate that reported efficiency gains for recurrent attention replacements must be stated relative to a named attention backend and a named implementation, and that hybridization is best justified on quality grounds.

items.title: KV Cache Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary:
KV cache quantization is well studied for autoregressive language models, where cached prefix states are exact under causal attention and quantization is mainly a cache reconstruction problem. Diffusion language models (dLLMs) break this assumption.

Fast dLLM inference reuses KV states across denoising steps, but bidirectional token representations can change as masked tokens are revealed, so the reused cache may already differ from full recomputation before quantization is applied. We study KV cache quantization under this cache-reuse error.

We adapt KIVI and KVQuant to Fast-dLLM-style prefix and dual cache reuse, and introduce TRACE and dLLM-KVQ. TRACE reconstructs feasible dLLM reveal trajectories from prompt-answer pairs, providing calibration states that match iterative masked decoding. dLLM-KVQ uses these trajectories to choose per-layer K-cache entries that remain in high precision according to output- and attention-level behavior metrics, while applying standard low-bit value quantization.

Across LLaDA and Dream evaluations on GSM8K, HumanEval, MATH, and MBPP, dLLM-KVQ achieves the highest average score among quantized methods across the reported 4-bit and 2-bit prefix/dual cache settings.

items.title: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions
items.summary:
Protocols combining single-qubit digital operations with analog quantum evolutions bypass large numbers of two-qubit entangling gates, offering a promising approach to variational algorithms and hybrid quantum simulation. Focusing on the digital-analog quantum neural network (DA-QNN) as a representative framework, this work demonstrates that incorporating long-range interactions enhances the efficiency of such hybrid algorithms.

Within the analog blocks, an Ising model with power-law interactions is employed to generate entanglement, and this protocol is benchmarked across supervised and unsupervised learning tasks. Beyond discussing the effects of the transverse field and evolution time, the primary analysis focuses on how the interaction range governs the expressibility and trainability of the ansatz.

For supervised image classification and many-body phase detection, long-range ansatzes match the performance of their short-range counterparts with fewer DA-QNN layers or shorter evolution times, owing to the rapid information propagation across the system enabled by nonlocal couplings. This resource reduction alleviates the classical optimization overhead and eases experimental implementation.

In unsupervised phase detection, although the long-range ansatz does not outperform its short-range counterpart in every regime, the two ansatzes provide complementary signatures that jointly reconstruct the complete phase diagram. These findings establish long-range interacting platforms as a compelling resource for advancing practical, large-scale digital-analog quantum computing.

items.title: A note on the ideal lattice of a weighted Leavitt path algebra
items.summary:
Let $K$ be a field and $L_K(E,w)$ the Leavitt path algebra of a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$. Suppose that $L_K(E,w)$ is not isomorphic to an ordinary Leavitt path algebra.

We prove that the ideal lattice of every countably generated unital $K$-algebra embeds as a closed interval into the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$. The embedding preserves multiplication of ideals modulo the lower endpoint of the interval.

It follows that the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$ is not distributive and that ideal multiplication in $L_K(E,w)$ is not commutative. Moreover, we show that if $(E,w)$ is countable, then $L_K(E,w)$ has exactly $|K|^{\aleph_0}$ ideals, prime ideals, left primitive ideals, and right primitive ideals.

items.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
items.summary:
We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions.

The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories.

In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

items.title: E.ON and Qoro Test Hybrid Quantum Computing for Energy Scheduling
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Qoro, E.ON and the UK National Quantum Computing Centre developed a proof of concept using hybrid quantum-classical computing to improve peer-to-peer energy transaction scheduling.

The team used Qoro’s Divi SDK and scheduler to decompose large grid optimisation problems into subproblems of up to 50 qubits, reducing quantum hardware execution time by approximately threefold through spatial circuit packing on IBM hardware.

The research found that QAOA sampling combined with classical feasibility repair reduced residual decomposition error compared with classical baselines, although the results remain a proof of concept rather than a demonstrated deployment in an operational power grid.

PRESS RELEASE — Qoro, E.ON , and the UK National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC) have successfully developed a proof-of-concept, exploring future applications of hybrid quantum-classical computing in peer-to-peer energy trading. With SparQ grant funding, the team developed a new decomposition-based optimisation pipeline, built using Qoro’s open-source software development kit (SDK), Divi, and orchestrated through Qoro’s scheduler. The resulting proof-of-concept improved upon previous hybrid methods using energy grid benchmark models, outperforming classical baselines. It also reduced hardware execution time by approximately 3x through spatial circuit packing on IBM quantum hardware. This proves that software orchestration can unlock utility-scale applications on today’s quantum processors.

By mathematically breaking the massive grid optimisation problem into smaller, more manageable pieces, the algorithm could reduce the energy transaction scheduling rounds (by reducing the solution decomposition length) to achieve high solution accuracy. In a real-world application, the solution decomposition length acts as ‘scheduling rounds’ that plan and coordinate energy transactions between grid users. By proving that the number of required rounds can be drastically reduced, these findings offer a near-term pathway for power grids to more efficiently manage complex energy transaction scheduling and ease grid strain.

This project was conducted with oversight from the STFC Hartree Centre and the NQCC through the SparQ 2025 programme, a UK national initiative supporting industry-led quantum computing projects focused on real-world applications. Earlier research by E.ON and the Hartree Centre laid the groundwork for this collaboration.

items.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
items.summary:
Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules.

In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules.

In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schröer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules.

In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

items.title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
items.summary: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

items.title: Niels Bohr Institute Spinout Pelagic Systems Targets Quantum Hardware Control
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Pelagic Systems, a spinout from the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme at the Niels Bohr Institute, is launching software for calibrating, monitoring and controlling quantum hardware.

The company says its platform has been demonstrated on superconducting quantum processors, where it can characterize and recalibrate key processor parameters on millisecond timescales.

Supported by Innovation Fund Denmark, Pelagic is offering its software to research groups and quantum computing companies working on advanced quantum hardware.

Pelagic Systems, a new spinout from the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute , was announced on October 27, 2026, according to a company press release. The company is developing the software layer for operating quantum hardware at the frontier.

Pelagic describes quantum processors as experimental systems that are delicate and constantly changing. Its platform brings tools to measure, understand and control them into a single software package, the release states. The company says that by closely integrating high-level experimental software with real-time hardware control, the platform makes possible a new generation of quantum experiments that can respond, adapt and explore the full potential of quantum hardware.

For Peter Krogstrup, CEO of NQCP and Quantum Foundry Copenhagen , Pelagic is an example of how technology developed around the programme’s quantum computing work can become capabilities with value well beyond a single research project, the release says. Krogstrup said in the release:

items.title: Formality transmission
items.summary:
Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences.

These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc.

In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission.

This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.

items.title: Local and 2-local derivations of Block Lie algebras B(q)
items.summary: We prove that every local or 2-local derivation of the Block Lie algebra $\B(q)$, with both basis indices in $\Z$, is a derivation for all $q\in\C$. The proofs use the known description of ordinary derivations, Laurent polynomials, and coefficient comparisons.

items.title: IQM Demonstrates Entanglement Across a Complete 54-Qubit Processor
items.summary:
Insider Brief

IQM Quantum Computers reports that its cloud-accessible Emerald system has achieved a Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) entangled state across all 54 qubits simultaneously.

The company measured a fidelity of 0.516 across the full processor with readout error mitigation applied, exceeding the 0.500 threshold cited for distinguishing genuine entanglement from noise.

IQM attributes the result to improvements in calibration, gate selection and automated state preparation, and says cloud customers can access the system’s full-chip performance.

PRESS RELEASE — IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX), a global leader in superconducting quantum computers, today announced that its cloud-accessible IQM Emerald system has fully entangled all 54 qubits on the chip simultaneously, a result that shows the system’s computational quality holds up when every qubit is put to work at once. IQM’s cloud customers now have access to that same full-chip performance, so their computations can draw on the entire processor rather than a fraction of it.

These results rank among the strongest reported for any commercially available quantum computer, giving customers access to state-of-the-art, high-quality processors. Until now, a user running a comparable demonstration on IQM Emerald could reliably use on the order of 30 qubits within a single algorithm. Studies on large quantum chips often use only a fraction of the available qubits, commonly 10 to 20, even when the hardware has many more. Emerald’s result shows the alternative: an entire processor working together on one computation.

“Entangling the entire chip means every qubit and every connection between them has to work correctly in the same circuit. Getting there came down to being smarter about how we prepare the state itself, choosing the gate order to keep idle time to a minimum,” said Craig Ciesla, CTO, IQM Quantum Computers. “Our current and prospective cloud customers now have the chance to benefit from the same tools and system performance that made this achievement possible.”

items.title: Pasqal’s 256-Qubit Processor Finds Unexpected Quantum Magnet Behavior
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Pasqal and its research collaborators used a 256-qubit neutral-atom processor to study a two-dimensional quantum magnet and observed an unexpected slowdown in its relaxation after a sudden change.

The slowdown appeared in a regime where three classical simulation methods diverged from one another and the experimental results, although the researchers have not yet explained the behavior.

The findings, published as an arXiv preprint, suggest quantum processors could help investigate complex physical systems that challenge existing simulation methods, but do not demonstrate computational quantum advantage.

PRESS RELEASE — Pasqal (Nasdaq: PSQL), a global leader in neutral-atom quantum computing, today announced that its 256-qubit quantum processor has revealed an unexpected behavior in a two-dimensional quantum magnet: under certain conditions, the system takes far longer to settle after being disturbed than theory predicts. The results, released as a preprint with the Flatiron Institute, the University of Augsburg, Forschungszentrum Jülich, the University of Regensburg and the Institut d’Optique–CNRS, were obtained in a regime where three state-of-the-art classical simulation methods no longer agree with one another.

A regime theory cannot yet predict

The researchers abruptly pushed the magnet out of equilibrium, a sudden change physicists call a quench and   expected it to settle quickly into a new stable state, as most systems do. Under one set of conditions, it didn’t. The result marks a shift in how quantum processors can be used in research: not only to reproduce what scientists already know, but to reveal behavior they did not anticipate.

items.title: Nord Quantique Secures $10 Million DARPA Funding Extension
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Nord Quantique has secured a US$10 million extension to its DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage B agreement to continue evaluation of its quantum computing architecture.

The company uses bosonic quantum error correction to protect quantum information within physical qubits, with the aim of reducing the hardware overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

DARPA ’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative evaluates whether emerging quantum architectures can reach utility-scale operation by 2033, while Nord Quantique says the funding will support its development roadmap.

PRESS RELEASE — Nord Quantique , a Canadian quantum computing company pioneering hardware-efficient quantum error correction, today announced a US$10 million extension of its Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency’s (DARPA) Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) Stage B agreement.

The extension supports Nord Quantique ’s continued participation in Stage B and its potential to deliver utility-scale quantum computing with significantly reduced hardware requirements.

DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative aims to determine whether emerging quantum computing architectures can achieve utility-scale operation by 2033. The program rigorously evaluates the technical feasibility, scalability and resources required to develop commercially valuable quantum computers.

items.title: On $κ$-existentially closed groups with few automorphisms
items.summary: We give constructions of $κ$-existentially closed groups having few automorphisms, giving negative solutions to a question of Kaya and Kuzucuoğlu in the Kourovka Notebook.

items.title: Large Ree groups acting point and line-primitively on finite generalised quadrangles
items.summary:
Suppose we have a finite thick generalised quadrangle whose automorphism group $G$ acts primitively on both the set of points and the set of lines.

Then $G$ must be almost simple.

Furthermore, $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 B_2(2^{2m+1})$ or ${}^2 G_2(3^{2m+1})$, where $m$ is a positive integer.

In this paper, we show that $\textrm{soc}(G)$ cannot be isomorphic to ${}^2 F_4(2^{2m+1})$.

items.title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
items.summary:
We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$.

We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$.

Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.

items.title: Shionogi Wins NEDO Award for Quantum-Assisted Drug Discovery
items.summary:
Insider Brief

D-Wave customer Shionogi has won first place in the Quality of Life category of Japan’s NEDO Challenge for research applying quantum computing to drug discovery.

A peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports in July 2026 found that a quantum-assisted generative AI model produced 97% chemically valid molecular representations, compared with 73% for an equivalent classical model.

The ¥40 million award will support Shionogi’s continued research combining quantum computing and classical high-performance computing to generate and evaluate potential drug candidates.

PRESS RELEASE — D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) (“ D-Wave “), the only dual-platform quantum computing company providing both annealing and gate-model systems, software and services, today announced that its customer Shionogi & Co., Ltd. (“Shionogi”) has won first place in the Quality of Life (QOL) category of the NEDO Challenge for its research exploring the application of quantum computing to drug discovery. The award-winning research includes, among other achievements, a peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports in July 2026, which integrated D-Wave annealing quantum computing technology into a generative AI model for molecular design.

Among the achievements included in the award-winning peer-reviewed research, conducted in collaboration with D-Wave , was that 97% of molecular representations generated by the quantum-assisted model were chemically valid, compared with 73% using an equivalent classical model. The quantum-assisted model also generated a higher proportion of molecules with strong drug-likeness scores, exceeding both the classical model and the training dataset. These findings demonstrate how annealing quantum computing could improve the quality of generative AI outputs for early-stage drug discovery.

The ¥40 million NEDO prize will support Shionogi’s continued research into applying quantum computing to one of the pharmaceutical industry’s most complex challenges: designing promising new drug candidate molecules. The award recognized Shionogi’s broader quantum-assisted drug discovery research, which combines D-Wave quantum computing and classical high-performance computing approaches to generate and evaluate drug candidate molecules.

items.title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
items.summary:
Let $Λ$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $Λ$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies.

The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $Λ$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules.

We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages.

Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension.

Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowroński--Waschbüsch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.

items.title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. Yet problem solving in unfamiliar domains calls for tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning, beyond factual retrieval and aggregation or learning solely from a preassembled context.

We study self-learning -- autonomously retrieving, studying, and applying knowledge from long-form reference materials on the fly. To investigate this capability, we formulate a textbook-based mathematical problem-solving task.

LLMs must navigate textbook exposition, learn and apply relevant principles, and construct proofs for exercises, with reference solutions withheld. We introduce a BookNavigator interface to support this human-inspired study process and incentivize self-learning through reinforcement learning (RL) with fine-grained rewards.

Experiments show that our method improves performance across in-domain and out-of-domain textbooks and subjects, raising Intern-S2-Preview-35B's overall proof accuracy from 51.5% to 79.5% and outperforming RL-trained textbook-free and fixed-retrieval baselines. These gains extend to complex long-context benchmarks involving different task types, with improvements over the base model of 1.7 and 2.3 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus and CL-bench, respectively.

Together, these findings suggest that RL can foster a domain-agnostic self-learning strategy, highlighting the potential of self-learning from long-form corpora to strengthen broader problem-solving capabilities on complex, long-context tasks.

items.title: Detection and Inhibition of Decoherence Through Collisions: A dynamical approach
items.summary:
Quantum systems are intrinsically fragile and highly vulnerable to environmental noise, making the preservation of quantum states one of the fundamental challenges in realizing practical quantum technologies. We propose two noise-agnostic quantum state protection protocols based on a collisional model.

The first protocol preserves quantum states of qubits without requiring complete prior knowledge of the underlying noise dynamics, and the second even protects a logical qubit under similar circumstances. These protocols provide robust protection for arbitrary single-qubit and entangled states against general noise processes.

Furthermore, their capability to safeguard quantum states with an arbitrary number of qubits enhances the reliability, robustness, and scalability of emerging quantum architectures. These results establish the proposed framework as a promising approach for practical quantum information processing.

items.title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
items.summary:
We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology.

Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N. Trung, and Vu concerning the stable value of the symbolic depth function, where the difference between the conjectured value and the actual value can be arbitrary large.

Finally, we study a conjecture of Muta stating the depth of a symbolic power of an edge ideal is at least that of the corresponding ordinary power. We prove it for graphs whose connected components are unicyclic or bipartite.

items.title: Automorphism groups of smooth quartic threefolds
items.summary:
We classify finite groups of automorphisms of smooth quartic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$.

Every such group embeds into one of $17$ maximal groups, which we realize by explicit equations and matrix generators.

Among finite subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(5,\mathbb{C})$ preserving a smooth quartic threefold, there are exactly $24$ maximal ones up to conjugacy, and we use them to determine the $194$ groups that occur as full automorphism groups.

As an application, we classify the finite groups of projective automorphisms of smooth quartic surfaces and show that there are exactly $12$ maximal ones up to conjugacy in $\mathrm{PGL}(4,\mathbb{C})$.

items.title: Patch release v5.21.1
items.summary: Patch release v5.21.1 ** Fix rope_scaling setter for configs that assign it during init ( #50080 ) We broke remote code loading in vllm, this fixes it sorry everyone!

items.title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
items.summary: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

items.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
items.summary:
We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others.

Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra. The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions.

When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups.

Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.

items.title: Adiabatic training of VQAs for entanglement detection
items.summary:
This paper introduces a hybrid quantum framework for training Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) aimed at addressing the fundamental problem of entanglement detection using adiabatic quantum computing. This problem is of foundational significance in quantum information science and has been approached through both classical and quantum methodologies.

We propose an adiabatic-inspired optimization strategy for training VQAs, which combines a discretization of the parameter space with a hierarchical segmentation scheme. The optimization problem is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model to leverage the capabilities of quantum annealing.

Preliminary results are compared against classical neural networks and conventional VQA training techniques. The findings aim to stimulate further investigation and discussion within the scientific community regarding the efficacy and applicability of the proposed approach.

items.title: Researchers Curb Unwanted Transitions in Ultrafast Quantum Gates
items.summary:
Insider Brief

Researchers from Jülich, Aachen and Cologne performed single-qubit operations in 6.8 nanoseconds with accuracies exceeding 99.98%, demonstrating fast, precise control of a superconducting qubit.

Their R2D pulse-shaping method reduced unwanted multiphoton transitions by more than 20 times compared with the established DRAG method.

Tests used a single isolated transmon qubit, with further experiments needed to assess performance in larger processors and two-qubit operations.

Image: Quantum computer laboratory at the Peter Grünberg Institute for Functional Quantum Systems (PGI-13) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. (Forschungszentrum Jülich / Sascha Kreklau)

PRESS RELEASE — Researchers from Jülich, Aachen and Cologne have performed a quantum operation on a qubit in just 6.8 nanoseconds – with more than 99.98 percent accuracy. Such operations typically take several tens of nanoseconds in superconducting quantum computers. The paper was published in Nature Communications .

6.8 nanoseconds – that’s how long it takes light to travel a distance of around two metres in a vacuum. In this tiny fraction of a second, researchers in the Peter Grünberg Institute for Functional Quantum Systems (PGI-13) and Quantum Control (PGI-8) at Forschungszentrum Jülich have succeeded in performing elementary computing operations on a quantum bit, or qubit for short.

items.title: Optimal Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulation for Dissipative Dynamics
items.summary:
Linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) is an efficient method for simulating dissipative dynamics on quantum computers.

The choice of the LCHS kernel controls the cost of the algorithm.

We prove that the kernel family proposed by Ni and Ying~\cite{NY26} minimizes the LCHS query cost in the minimax sense.

For target accuracy $ε$, the minimum cost is asymptotically $\frac{2\mathrm{e}}π(\ln\frac1ε-\ln\ln\frac1ε+o(1))$, with optimal leading constant $\frac{2\mathrm{e}}π$.

Our lower-bound proof combines weak duality with a realization lemma that approximates extremal dual functions by matrix elements of dissipative evolutions.

items.title: Poincaré series of degree-two Chow varieties
items.summary:
Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees.

An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. We identify the ordinary Poincaré polynomial with the known virtual formula, determine the optimal ranges over which the coefficients stabilize, and compute the nonrational Poincaré series of the stable space $D(2)$.

For the Lawson--Michelsohn map $D(2)\longrightarrow D(\infty)$, the first nonzero rational homotopy kernel occurs in degree eight and is one-dimensional, while the integral kernel has rank one. Finally, we compute the relative homology of the pair $(D(2),BU)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ and show that additional cohomology generators and nonzero rational homotopy kernels arise in unbounded degrees.

items.title: Automated Verification of Hamiltonian Simulation by Quantum Signal Processing
items.summary:
We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first fully automated verification framework for QSP-based Hamiltonian simulation. Our framework exploits the structure of the simulation algorithm: Hamiltonians are given as weighted sums of Pauli strings, embedded into larger unitaries through block encodings, and transformed into time-evolution operators by quantum signal processing (QSP).

Using a symbolic Pauli-sum semantics for ancilla-indexed circuit blocks, our verifier proves that the distinguished all-zero ancilla block is proportional to the target Hamiltonian and infers the subnormalization factor automatically. It then verifies the QSP layer by extracting the implemented polynomial transformation and certifying its approximation error.

This structure-aware abstraction is essential for scalability. Composing our verified block encoding and QSP wrapper yields an estimated macro-expanded size of about 1.52 million gates.

The verifier certifies the block encoding once and checks the QSP layer through its abstract interface, without expanding the oracle calls. Our implementation verifies block encodings of structured Pauli-sum Hamiltonians with up to 256 system qubits and verifies QSP Hamiltonian-simulation instances by extracting their implemented polynomials and checking the resulting approximation bounds.

These results show that fully automated verification can handle common Hamiltonian-simulation circuits at substantial scale when it exploits their algorithmic structure.

items.title: Epimorphism testing with dihedral targets
items.summary:
We consider the problem of deciding whether or not there is an epimorphism from the class of finitely presented groups to a fixed finite group.

We show this problem is $\mathsf{NP}$-complete when the target is a non-nilpotent dihedral group.

This complements work of Kuperberg and Samperton (2018, Geom.

Topol.) who showed the same result when the target is a fixed finite non-abelian simple group.

We also include a survey of complexity and reduction results when the source and target are classes of finitely presented groups.

items.title: Topology Survives Shuffling: Robust Long-Context Memory Access Prediction for Graph Analytics
items.summary:
Graph analytics generates irregular, topology-dependent memory-access streams via indirect traversals, limiting data prefetching. Accurate prediction enables timely prefetches that hide memory latency. However, ML predictors couple short histories with fixed horizons, fitting the training trace's node layout rather than learning transferable graph patterns.

We propose LoCoMAP, a long-context representation-learning framework for memory-access prediction with independently controlled observation history and prediction horizon. We evaluate Connected Components (CC), PageRank (PR), and Single-Source Shortest Paths (SSSP) on six synthetic graph families, with Erdos-Renyi (ER) and Grid as random and deterministic controls. We test two interventions: same-family regeneration changes connectivity, while node shuffling disrupts layout but preserves connectivity.

Across 18 graph-workload pairs, extending history from 8 to 128 accesses improves F1 by 7.8%, while extending prediction horizon from 8 to 512 improves F1 by 88.3%. For CC, regeneration is less disruptive than shuffling: without retraining, long context retains 95.4% of original F1 and outperforms short context in six families. Under full shuffle, long context improves CC F1 by 33.6% across ER, Barabasi-Albert, Copying Model, and Stochastic Block Model (SBM), with a 2.06x gain on SBM, but not on Watts-Strogatz or Grid, where near-zero delta mass shifts into heavy tails beyond the predictor's range.

Long context outperforms short context on six real-world CC graphs. At full shuffle, long-context PR retains 57.6% of original F1 and averages 11.0% above short context. Both SSSP models retain about 30% of original F1 under full shuffle as distance updates access vertex data in a new order.

Within these bounds, long-context predictors are robust across related graphs and layouts without retraining, enabling a generalizable graph prefetcher.

items.title: SeQUeNCe.DQC: Full-stack Simulation of Distributed Quantum Computing
items.summary:
Distributed quantum computing (DQC) connects multiple quantum processing units to overcome the scale limits of monolithic hardware. We introduce SeQUeNCe.DQC, a new top-level module within the SeQUeNCe package that compiles monolithic circuits into topology-aware execution plans and coordinates their execution using SeQUeNCe's existing quantum-network modules and protocols.

We validate SeQUeNCe.DQC by reproducing a two-node trapped-ion Grover experiment in simulation and comparing success probabilities with the reported 71% benchmark. We then evaluate how compiler strategy, topology, and memory capacity jointly govern distributed circuit execution time and success rate.

In these experiments, our hybrid compilers successfully identified mixed TeleGate/TeleData execution plans that outperformed pure gate-teleportation strategies. By capturing the physical overhead of distributed quantum primitives, SeQUeNCe.DQC provides a rigorous platform for co-designing DQC software and hardware architectures.

items.title: Subindices of two-element subsets of finite groups
items.summary:
Let $A$ be a nonempty subset of a group $G$. A right subfactor relative to $A$ is a subset $B$ maximal under inclusion among those for which every element of $AB$ has a unique representation as $ab$, with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$. Left subfactors are defined analogously using $BA$. The infima and suprema of the cardinalities of right and left subfactors define four \emph{subindices}. A subset is called \emph{index-stable} if its four subindices coincide.

For any infinite group $G$, every nonempty finite subset of $G$ is index-stable.

For finite groups, the situation is more complicated. We prove that for a two-element subset of a finite group, the left and right subindices coincide pairwise. Let $A=\{x,y\}$ with $x\ne y$, and let $X$ be the cyclic subgroup generated by $x^{-1}y$. Then the lower subindex of $A$ is $|G:X|\cdot\lceil |X|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is $|G:X|\cdot\lfloor |X|/2\rfloor$. These formulas imply that $A$ is index-stable if and only if $|X|$ is one of $2,3,4,5,7$.

For any two-element subset of a finite group $G$, the lower subindex is at least $\lceil |G|/3\rceil$, and the upper subindex is at most $\lfloor |G|/2\rfloor$. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in each of these bounds.

All two-element subsets of a finite group are index-stable if and only if every element of the group has order $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, $5$, or $7$. We give a complete structural classification of such groups.

items.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
items.summary: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.

items.title: Softmax Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models: Collapse and Recovery
items.summary:
Softmax routing in mixture-of-experts models can concentrate probability on a subset of experts, suppressing access to the others. We study how this concentration forms, why it persists, and how suppressed probabilities recover.

For fixed experts, a stationary-loss barrier identifies the face supporting the optimal routed output. In a common-target square-loss model with freely trainable expert outputs, slow adaptation tracks fixed-expert dynamics on finite horizons, while every fixed positive adaptation rate yields an interior routing limit.

An exact normal-velocity decomposition separates complementary-expert covariance from relative gradient advantage. Under positive two-sided power bounds along recovery paths, uniform over initial masses, the resulting coefficient's order of vanishing gives logarithmic or power-law recovery times.

Integrations of constructed fields reproduce these orders. An exact discrete log-odds identity relates neural updates to threshold crossing.

In paired Transformer-MoE training, removing a class-conditional router-gradient contrast delays confirmed recovery and reduces accumulated log-odds on fixed tokens, both with and without capacity constraints.

items.title: LinQuant: Functional Invariances for Low-Precision Linear Recurrences
items.summary:
Linear recurrences are emerging as practical alternatives to softmax attention in large language models, appearing in both standalone and hybrid architectures. However, despite their rapid emergence, low-precision inference remains much less developed for these models than for softmax attention.

During prefill, chunkwise-parallel algorithms cast much of the recurrence as dense matrix multiplications, suggesting a natural path to low-precision execution. Simply quantizing these operations in their native form, however, can be fragile.

In this work, we identify functional invariances that preserve the full-precision computation while making the operands more amenable to quantization. Building on this observation, we introduce LinQuant, a framework for low-precision recurrent prefill based on seven such invariances, including rotations, diagonal rescalings, and alternative placements of recurrent decay and write factors.

We derive when these transformations remain valid across common recurrence families spanning linear, gated, and delta-rule updates, and show that they provide complementary degrees of freedom for improving low-precision accuracy. Finally, we translate this framework to production by augmenting SSDi8, an existing low-precision prefill pipeline for Mamba-2, with the applicable invariances.

LinQuant improves perplexity at matched latency on Mamba-2 1.3B, 2.7B, and 8B and Nemotron-H 8B, demonstrating the practical utility of invariance-based quantization for recurrent models.

items.title: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification
items.summary:
We derive analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian, governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the calculation reorganizes the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, yielding directly evaluable expressions for all 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order correlations.

The construction uses no parametric approximation or fitted parameters. Representative numerical benchmarks show errors of order $10^{-12}$ throughout the entire pump depletion, and below $10^{-3}$ across dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles, up to the first total collapse of the oscillation.

The first-depletion treatment additionally provides 4th-order correlations, accommodates bright squeezed-pump inputs and reveals phenomena important to future optical quantum technologies. The framework can be extended to higher moments.

items.title: Cord: Confidence-Anchored Order Residual Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary:
The decoding order of masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) can substantially affect generation quality, yet common decoders typically apply the same reveal rule throughout generation. Confidence provides a strong default, but it measures how decisively a position can be predicted now, not how useful revealing that position will be for subsequent decoding.

We propose Cord, a lightweight prompt-conditioned policy that retains confidence decoding as a stable reference and learns when and how to depart from it through geometric residuals over generation direction, proximity to revealed context, and two-sided infilling. The residuals adapt to both the prompt and the evolving partial response.

Rather than sampling a new policy action at every decoding step, Cord samples a single low-dimensional coefficient matrix per rollout, which induces an entire state-dependent reveal trajectory. This yields a contextual-bandit formulation trained directly from sequence-level rewards, without step-level credit assignment or backbone updates.

Across three dLLMs and five reasoning, code, and constraint-satisfaction benchmarks, Cord improves average task success from 32.0% under confidence decoding to 48.2%, and further improves over the best per-domain fixed residual. Behavioral audits show that the learned residuals induce substantial, task-dependent changes in reveal locality and two-sided infilling.

Cord adds only $0.53$M trainable parameters, requires no additional backbone forward passes, and incurs only 5.39% inference latency overhead.

items.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
items.summary:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two.

Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle.

More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic Néron--Severi lattice.

The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$.

Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles.

items.title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
items.summary:
We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{λ,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $λ\ne1$.

No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $λ$.

Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices.

We give the precise parameter conditions for these two involutions.

As an application, we also determine the full automorphism group when the multiplicative group generated by the parameters is torsion-free.

items.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
items.summary:
We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$.

Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$.

This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length.

The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

items.title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
items.summary:
In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time.

On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny.

For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement.

An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.

items.title: Tensor products of Leibniz bimodules and Grothendieck rings -- an addendum
items.summary:
We continue our investigation of certain associativity properties (namely, alternativity, power-associativity, or being a Jordan ring) of the non-associative multiplication defined on the Grothendieck group of the category of finite-dimensional Leibniz bimodules which we started in \cite{FW}.

Namely, we prove that for every finite-dimensional non-zero Leibniz algebra over an arbitrary field this Grothendieck ring is not power-associative.

As a consequence, the Grothendieck ring is also neither alternative nor a Jordan ring.

This corrects and generalizes some of our results in the last section of \cite{FW}.

items.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
items.summary:
Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction.

We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold.

Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities. We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus.

Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

items.title: On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets
items.summary:
Daniel Carter , Kevin O’Bryant , and I have uploaded to the arXiv our paper On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets . This is a paper stemming from an interaction on my blog last year , regarding the use of AlphaEvolve to improve the then state of the art on the size of Sidon sets. We obtained a series of further refinements to the bound until progress stalled; after several months of no further progress, we decided to release what we have in this preprint.

Recall that a Sidon set is a set of integers with the property that all the sums with and are distinct. Equivalently, all the differences , are distinct, except at where of course there is a large multiplicity. A basic question ( Erdős problem #30 ) asks for the largest size of a Sidon set in . Several algebraic constructions of Sidon sets (by Singer, Bose, and Ruzsa) are known with and special choices of ; see this survey of O’Bryant for details. Erdős and Turán have conjectured that cannot exceed , with the bound also proposed by Erdős as “perhaps too optimistic”.

Very recently, a slightly sharper bound of 0.942809522 was obtained by a different method , but our focus here is on the method rather than the specific numerical constant obtained. (We also did not try to use 2026-level AI tools to optimize our own bound.)

To illustrate our approach, let us sketch a proof of the bound (1) . The fact that all the non-zero differences of are disjoint gives rise to a pointwise convolution bound
